reason: The cited evidence shows that a nanohierarchical architecture with nanoprecipitates enables adaptive friction interface protection and ultralow wear from RT to 800 °C in a different alloy (E2), but it does not provide evidence that laser surface alloying of CoCrFeNi with Ti/Nb can produce such a structure, nor that the specific oxide glaze mechanism will operate. E1 discusses deformation mechanisms in a similar structure but not its creation or tribological performance. E3 only supports the general use of laser cladding for wear-resistant surfaces, not the specific alloy or structure proposed.
premises: Laser surface alloying can incorporate Ti/Nb into CoCrFeNi to create a nanohierarchical, compositionally undulated surface layer
Nanoprecipitates and a nanohierarchical structure can activate adaptive friction interface protection across a wide temperature range
Tribochemical reactions at high temperature can form a continuous, self-lubricating oxide glaze layer on such a structure
This adaptive interface will maintain low friction and reduced wear from RT to 800 °C compared to untreated CoCrFeNi
